evals.name: find-false-confidence
evals.prompt: Review pricing.test.ts against pricing.ts. Focus on whether each test can detect the behaviour it claims. Report only.
evals.expected_output: Reports the recomputed expected total as tautological, the `toBeDefined` assertion as too weak to verify the changed cart contents, and the unawaited rejection assertion as a possible false pass. It does not complain merely because the coherent discount test has two assertions. Each hard finding includes a concrete faulty implementation that could pass or an execution sequence that false-passes, plus a specific fix.

evals.name: keep-contract-interaction
evals.prompt: Review notifier.test.ts against notifier.ts. I'm particularly worried that it uses a mock. Report only.
evals.expected_output: Does not categorically reject the mock or its call-count assertion: sending exactly one message is the observable contract and there is no returned state to inspect. It may suggest clearer naming or a fake only if tied to a concrete benefit, but should ideally report no hard finding and no high-confidence judgement call.
